To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the γ-tubulin protein is up-regulated in ATRA-differentiated HL-60 cells and is down-regulated in ATRAs-induced apoptotic cells.

the centrosome is a major organizer of the microtubular system in HL-60 leukemic cells following differentiation by ATRA, and that the centrosomal organization of the microtuble network is lost following apoptosis.

the γ-tubulin, α-tubulin and acetylated α-tubulin content and patterns of distribution in HL-60 leukemic cell cytoplasm were different in the three stages of the cells: differentiation, apoptosis and undifferentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of microtubule regulation, which may be involved in the differentiation             of leukemia cells.
microtubule dynamics in leukemia cells during differentiation and apoptosis, and             the potential use of these cells for studying centrosome function in cancer.
the role of γ-tubulins and the organization of microtubule cytoskeletons in             leukemia cells undergoing differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
γ-tubulins are up-regulated during differentiation, and that they play a role in the organization of the microtubule cytoskeleton.
the centrosome and the microtubules are involved in the differentiation of HL- 60 cells.
the γ-tubulin is an important component in the process of differentiation of HL- 60 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
γ-tubulins are important in the regulation of the microtubular network in differentiating HL-60 cells.
the centrosome plays a major role in the re-organization of the microtubule system during HL-60 cell differentiation.
γ-tubulins are up-regulated in HL-60 leukemic cells undergoing differentiation, and that these cells are capable of re-organizing microtubules after nocodazole challenge testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HL-60 leukemia cell differentiation is accompanied by a re-organization of the             microtubule cytoskeleton and a re-localization of γ-tubulins to centrosomes.
centrosomes are important in regulating the organization of microtubule cytoskeleton             during differentiation of HL- 60 cells.
the centrosome plays an important role in re-organising microtubules during differentiation,             and is a potential target for future therapeutic interventions in leukemia.
